handoffs.message: Review commits fa605aeca and b0bfbbda8 (branch includes origin/dev sync): deterministic source-agnostic materializer, scoped typed reverse index/RBAC filter, graph, quality diagnostics, rebuild/watermarks; duplicate/out-of-order/late/correction/replace/partial-fill/cancel/mismatch/failure coverage. Verification after dev sync: 25 passed; py_compile and diff-check passed.

Review found a correctness bug: JourneyMaterializer._sort_key (materializer.py) orders events by the normalized occurred_at STRING. _normalize preserves whatever fractional-second precision the source event used (datetime.isoformat() omits microseconds when absent), so an event at 00:00:00Z (no micros) sorts AFTER an event at 00:00:00.500000Z (with micros) even though the no-micros event is chronologically earlier or equal. Repro: rebuild([event(e1,...,'2026-07-12T00:00:00Z'), event(e2,...,'2026-07-12T00:00:00.500000Z')]) yields timeline order [e2, e1] and swaps snapshot created_at/updated_at. This breaks the deterministic out-of-order/late-event ordering that is this task's core acceptance criterion whenever producers differ in timestamp precision. Fix: sort by the parsed datetime (or normalize occurred_at to a fixed fractional-second width, e.g. isoformat(timespec='microseconds')) instead of comparing raw strings of differing length, and add a regression test mixing microsecond and whole-second timestamps for the same journey. Existing 7 tests all use uniform whole-second timestamps so they do not catch this. Please fix and hand back for re-review.

Reviewer timestamp-ordering bug fixed in edee66dd8: occurred_at is normalized to fixed-width UTC microseconds, preserving chronological timeline and source-watermark ordering across producer precision; mixed whole/fractional-second regression added. Verification: 8 passed; py_compile and git diff --check passed. Please re-review.

Round 2 review: timestamp-ordering fix in edee66dd8 verified correct via independent re-derivation of the pre-fix lexicographic bug and re-run of the regression test; 8 passed, py_compile clean, git diff --check clean. Approved and handed back to owner for closeout.
